title: vtec_adapter_connection_status reports distinct, correct adapter and target labels
description: RegisterAdapter(name, target, adapter) stores the real network endpoint (e.g. ldap.corp.local:636) separately from the operator's instance name (e.g. corp-ad-01) — regression coverage for a Phase 1 bug where both labels collapsed to the same value.
preconditions: Two fake adapters registered with distinct names and targets, one healthy and one not
expectedResult: vtec_adapter_connection_status{adapter="healthy-one",target="ldap.corp.local:636"} 1 and {adapter="unhealthy-one",target="sql.corp.local:1433"} 0 both appear with distinct target values.

title: Cached mTLS certificate and envelope signing key survive a process restart
description: cache.Open on the same BoltDB file across two process lifetimes must return the identical certificate/key material stored by the first — this is what lets a restarted connector skip re-registration.
preconditions: A cache opened, populated with a cert + signing key, then closed
steps: Load the certificate and signing key
expectedResult: Both values load back byte-identical to what was stored, with no re-registration triggered.

title: Rotator.OnRotate fires every registered subscriber, not just the first
description: OnRotate is a slice, not a single-slot field — a second subscriber (e.g. the cert-expiry metrics gauge) registered after websocket.Client.UpdateCertificate must still fire on every rotation.
preconditions: A Rotator with two independent OnRotate callbacks registered against a real (test) renewal server
expectedResult: Both callbacks are invoked with the newly-issued certificate, in registration order.

title: Enqueue -> Next -> Ack permanently removes a message from the JetStream buffer
preconditions: An embedded NATS JetStream queue started against a temp store dir
steps: Call Ack() on the fetched message
expectedResult: The second Next() call times out with no message — the acked item is never redelivered.

title: Nak triggers redelivery up to MaxDeliver, then the message is dead-lettered
steps: Fetch and Nak the same message 5 times in a row
expectedResult: After the 5th Nak, the message moves to the dead-letter stream and is no longer returned by Next() on the primary consumer.

title: AppRole login + KV-v2 write/read round trip returns the exact stored credential value
preconditions: A real (dev fixture) Vault instance with the vtec AppRole configured
expectedResult: The read returns exactly the written value; a read for a nonexistent ref returns null, not an error.

title: A WS heartbeat envelope writes cpu/memory/queue_depth into vtec_connector_metrics
description: HeartbeatService.recordHeartbeat persists every heartbeat sample (not just the latest onto ConnectorDoc) so GET /connectors/{id}/status can read a fresh, real value.
preconditions: A registered test connector and a real heartbeat envelope payload
steps: Send a heartbeat envelope over the mTLS WS connection
expectedResult: A new document appears with the exact cpu_percent/memory_mb/queue_depth values from the envelope and a fresh timestamp.

title: Scheduler fires an adapter's configured cron schedule and reports a StepSucceeded result
preconditions: An adapter registered with schedule "@every 1s" against a runner that returns a successful collection
steps: Register the adapter with the scheduler
Wait for at least one tick
expectedResult: OnResult fires with Steps containing one entry for the adapter, Status=StepSucceeded, and a non-nil Collection.

title: Pipeline.Run executes all 8 synchronous stages in wiki §06 order and stops cleanly on an intentional drop
preconditions: A Pipeline built from real Normalize/Filter/Dedupe/Mask/Enrich/Compress/Encrypt/Queue stages
steps: Run a fresh record through the pipeline
Run the identical record through the same pipeline a second time
expectedResult: The stages execute in the exact order Normalize->Filter->Dedupe->Mask->Enrich->Compress->Encrypt->Queue; the second run returns (nil, nil) at Dedupe with no error and no later stage executes.

title: First Snapshot() call after construction reports a sane CPU percentage, not a startup spike
description: ProcessMetricsSource takes a baseline sample at construction time specifically so the first real Snapshot() diffs against that baseline rather than zero, which would otherwise divide the process's entire cumulative CPU-seconds by a near-zero elapsed interval.
expectedResult: CPUPercent is a small, plausible value (not thousands of percent) on the very first call.
